events.gate: Caller entry — no internal precondition beyond FAILED rejection.
Delivered as the successful outcome of an asynchronous connection attempt. The gate is the completion of `_attempt_connection()` without exception.
Delivered as the failure outcome of an asynchronous connection attempt.
Delivered as the timeout outcome of an asynchronous connection attempt.
Delivered when `asyncio.sleep(backoff + jitter)` completes in the retry loop.
Internal check `retry_count >= max_retries` after increment in `_connect_loop`.

docLines.target: SYS-01: `connect()` sets state to CONNECTING and starts a connection attempt
SYS-02: `disconnect()` sets `_should_stop=True`, cancels pending tasks, sets state to DISCONNECTED
SYS-03: On successful connection, state=CONNECTED and retry_count=0
SYS-04: On connection failure, retry_count increments, component retries up to max_retries with exponential backoff + jitter
SYS-05: When retry_count >= max_retries, state=FAILED; no further connection attempts
SYS-06: Connection timeout is treated as a failure (caught in same except block, device_connection.py:111)
SYS-07: retry_count=0 already set on successful connect; min_uptime timer started
SYS-08: Backoff computed as `base_backoff * 2^(retry_count-1) + uniform(0, backoff*0.5)`

connect.loss: n/a: direct synchronous call; loss means caller never invokes, which is outside the component boundary.
connect.delay: n/a: synchronous call with no timeout semantics at the boundary.
connect.duplication: UV-connect-dup — caller invokes `connect()` twice in rapid succession.
connect.out-of-order: n/a: single caller; ordering relative to other events is covered by interaction pairs.
connect.contradiction: UV-connect-contra — `connect()` and `disconnect()` called simultaneously from separate coroutines.
connect.commission: UV-connect-commission — spurious `connect()` call when already CONNECTED (no-op path).
connect.value: n/a: `connect()` takes no parameters that could carry a foreign session or stale epoch.

disconnect.loss: n/a: direct synchronous call; loss means caller never invokes, outside the component boundary.
disconnect.delay: n/a: synchronous call with no timeout semantics at the boundary.
disconnect.duplication: UV-disconnect-dup — caller invokes `disconnect()` twice in rapid succession.
disconnect.out-of-order: n/a: single caller; ordering covered by interaction pairs.
disconnect.contradiction: UV-disconnect-contra — `disconnect()` and `connect()` called simultaneously from separate coroutines.
disconnect.commission: UV-disconnect-commission — spurious `disconnect()` call when already DISCONNECTED.

connection_succeeds.loss: UV-conn-succeeds-loss — the success callback is lost (task cancelled, event loop stopped).
connection_succeeds.delay: UV-conn-succeeds-delay — the success arrives after `disconnect()` has already cancelled the task.
connection_succeeds.duplication: UV-conn-succeeds-dup — the success event fires twice (unlikely given single-task pattern, but task resurrection or double-completion is a UV).
connection_succeeds.out-of-order: UV-conn-succeeds-stale — a stale success from a previously cancelled `_connect_task` arrives after a new `connect()` has been issued.
connection_succeeds.contradiction: n/a: success and failure cannot co-occur on the same attempt.
connection_succeeds.commission: n/a: success requires a preceding connection attempt.
connection_succeeds.value: n/a: success has no payload carrying entity identity.

connection_fails.loss: UV-conn-fails-loss — the failure callback is lost (task cancelled, exception swallowed).
connection_fails.delay: UV-conn-fails-delay — the failure arrives after `disconnect()` has already cancelled the task.
connection_fails.duplication: UV-conn-fails-dup — the failure event fires twice.
connection_fails.out-of-order: UV-conn-fails-stale — a stale failure from a cancelled task arrives out of order.
connection_fails.contradiction: n/a: success and failure cannot co-occur on the same attempt.
connection_fails.commission: n/a: failure requires a preceding connection attempt.
connection_fails.value: n/a: failure carries no entity-identifying payload.

connection_timeout.loss: UV-conn-timeout-loss — the timeout is swallowed or the task is cancelled before the timeout fires.
connection_timeout.delay: UV-conn-timeout-delay — the timeout fires late, after a new connection has already been initiated.
connection_timeout.out-of-order: UV-conn-timeout-stale — a stale timeout from a cancelled task arrives out of order.
connection_timeout.contradiction: n/a: timeout and success cannot co-occur on the same attempt.
connection_timeout.commission: n/a: timeout requires a preceding connection attempt.
connection_timeout.value: n/a: timeout carries no entity-identifying payload.

backoff_elapsed.loss: UV-backoff-loss — the sleep is interrupted by task cancellation before completing.
backoff_elapsed.delay: UV-backoff-delay — the sleep takes longer than expected (e.g., event loop congestion).
backoff_elapsed.duplication: n/a: a single sleep completion is atomic.
backoff_elapsed.out-of-order: n/a: backoff is sequential within the loop; ordering violation requires loop corruption.
backoff_elapsed.contradiction: n/a: no simultaneous contradictory event possible for a timer completion.
backoff_elapsed.commission: UV-backoff-commission — a spurious wakeup from `asyncio.sleep` (theoretical; Python asyncio does not spurious-wake).

max_retries_exhausted.loss: n/a: this is a synchronous check, not a delivered event; it cannot be lost.
max_retries_exhausted.duplication: n/a: synchronous check evaluated once per failure.
max_retries_exhausted.out-of-order: n/a: synchronous check in the same control flow.
max_retries_exhausted.contradiction: n/a: synchronous check cannot contradict itself.
max_retries_exhausted.commission: n/a: requires a preceding failure and increment; cannot occur spontaneously.
max_retries_exhausted.value: UV-maxretries-value — `max_retries` is misconfigured (0 or negative) or `retry_count` is corrupted, causing premature or skipped exhaustion.
